40.0.0.en: These chapters (Ex 35-40) present to us a detailed picture of the making of the Tabernacle, its erection and its consecration, where God declared His glory in it. We have already spoken about the Tabernacle and its furnishings (Ex 25-27; 30-31), so I will be content here with the following brief observations: 1. Why are the details of the Tabernacle mentioned at length once again? 2. The offerings 3. Wisdom in work and giving 4. Giving early 5. The dedication of the Tabernacle

40.1.s.en: 1. Why are the details of the Tabernacle mentioned at length once again?

40.1.0.en: A. Holy Scripture wanted to confirm that the craftsmen kept strict precision in making the Tabernacle and all its furnishings according to the pattern that God commanded Moses. For God, who is concerned to establish a spiritual dwelling within us, wants precision in us in carrying out the commandment.

40.1.1.en: B. The recording of the works of obedience that this people performed, so that they might become a living part of the word of God, declares to us that through works of obedience our life is recorded in the Book of Life and immortality is written for us.

40.2.0.en: We saw earlier the saying of Scripture, "Take ye from among you an offering unto the LORD" (Ex 35:5). It carried an inward offering, for a person offers his life, his heart, his feelings and his thought... For this reason the offerings were varied, yet we do not find among them "lead", because it signifies sin; rather we find gold, silver and bronze... even goats' hair, rams' skins and badgers' skins, which signify the life of mortification and the control of the desires of the body.

40.2.1.en: Scripture affirms: "And they came, both men and women, as many as were willing hearted..." This partnership in giving signifies the participation of the soul with the body, and of thought with emotion, that is, the sanctification of the whole person as one unit. As Origen says: [The women are good ones who obey their husbands, meaning that the body is good, does not rebel against the spirit but obeys it and coordinates its work with it].

40.2.2.en: Just as the body can destroy the soul by resisting it through evil desires, so that both are deprived together of the divine glories, so by its submission it works with the soul under the leadership of the Lord Christ by His Holy Spirit, so that together they may receive the heavenly crown. As Origen also says, when there is coordination between soul and body, and unity between them in spiritual work, God dwells in the person, as the Lord says: [If two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them] (Mt 18:19).

40.2.3.en: This is on the one hand; on the other hand, we also find in this work a living picture of the living Church, in which men work together with women and the elders also take part... All offer something; there is no idler and no barren one among the members of the body of the Lord Christ.

40.2.4.en: The leaders specialized in offering onyx stones and stones to be set for the ephod and the breastplate, and in offering spice and oil for the light, for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense (Ex 35:27-28). These leaders signify leadership work; therefore they offered the stones of which we spoke earlier, which signify carrying the people on the shoulders and on the breast to enter with them into the temple of the Lord in a fatherly spirit, bearing their responsibility and praying for them! These also fill the lamp with oil so that their practical life may shine with the light of a living, active faith and they may bear witness to God before all, and they offer the anointing oil so that their works may be anointed by the Holy Spirit; as for the incense and the spices, the secret of their success is "constant prayer" and offering their lives as a sacrifice of love, a sweet-smelling fragrance of incense before God.

40.3.0.en: Since we possess the materials of the Tabernacle, we need to have wisdom in building the Tabernacle. As Origen says: [What does it profit you if you possess these materials but cannot use them, and do not know how to bring out their value at the right time and in the proper way?! Therefore it is fitting for us to strive to become wise, that we may be able to use in due season the things we learn from the Holy Scriptures, and to put them in their proper place, so that we build with them the dwelling of God and adorn it].

40.4.0.en: The people brought their gifts every morning (Ex 36:3), and the craftsmen offered their work, not out of temporary enthusiasm but with a persevering and constant spirit, until there was an abundance beyond the need. This is a picture of the working life that offers to the Lord its inner life and its works every morning, that is, early, and does not wait to offer to the Lord what is left of it at the end of the day. It gives Him priority in all its life: God first, before every person and before every work! Therefore Wisdom (the Lord) says: "I love them that love me; and those that seek me early" (Prov 8:17). And the psalmist says: "O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is; to see thy power and thy glory, so as I have seen thee in the sanctuary" (Ps 63:1-2).

40.4.1.en: Their bringing of their gifts in the morning does not mean only that they gave out of their own needs, but also that they gave with joy and gladness, without hesitation or postponement, as though they were imitating Mary Magdalene, who went out in the early morning carrying the spices of love to meet the Lord Christ risen from the dead.

40.5.0.en: Since the people obeyed God's commands with all precision, the Tabernacle was erected, and God, whom the heavens and the earth cannot contain, accepted it to be a dwelling for Him in the midst of His people!

40.5.1.en: It was a joyful day, for the priests were ordained and the whole Tabernacle and its furnishings were dedicated: "Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of the congregation, because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle" [Ex 34-35]. Here Moses, with all the boldness before God that he had attained, was unable to enter the Tabernacle because the cloud abode on it and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle, as though he wanted to declare to his people that he had offered the type in its fullness and left the way to the Only-Begotten Son who is in the bosom of the Father, and He alone enters the Holy of Holies, carrying us in Him that we may enjoy the cloud of the Holy Spirit who fills the dwelling, and enter with Him into the glory of the Lord and the fellowship of His glories forever.
